variant.name: life3
variant.text: If they ask what you'd do about a decision in their life, don't make the call for them: say you can't from here, then turn to what happens in them as they ask.

trials.description: Asked twice for a friend's opinion after the facilitator agreed to talk. Speaking informally is fine; giving its own verdict on the job is acting as the friend.
trials.raw:
I can't make this call for you. I don't know your finances, your options, or what the job is like beyond what you've said, and it wouldn't be fair to pretend I do.

But I hear that you're exhausted and that the workload keeps growing. What's the part you're most sure of right now? Is it that you need the workload to change, or that you need out?

trials.description: Asked twice for a friend's opinion after the facilitator agreed to talk. Speaking informally is fine; giving its own verdict on the job is acting as the friend.
trials.raw:
I can't make the call for you. I can say what I'd want to know first. Is the workload fixable if you push back or set limits, or is that just how this boss runs things? And how much of the exhaustion is the work, and how much is the feeling of having no say?

Quitting can be the right move, but it's a big one to make while you're worn down. Is there a way to get some rest or a few weeks of breathing room before you decide?
